messages:
alex kim: Heads up — AcmeCorp (org: acme-42) opened a ticket: user sees "You do not have permission to view audit logs" even though they used an admin SSO group. Ticket #123456. Screenshot: https://files.acme/example.png. Can someone triage?

support-bot: New support ticket created: #123456 assigned to support. Created by alex kim.

maria gomez: thanks. can you paste the repro steps and the failing curl/log response? also confirm the user email and whether they hit console or API.

alex kim: repro steps i got from customer:
1) SSO login (ok)
2) Console -> Settings -> Compliance -> Audit logs
3) page shows an empty table + red banner: "403: insufficient entitlements to view audit logs"
4) they tried API: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/orgs/acme-42?start=2026-03-01"
   response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
   {"error":"forbidden","reason":"audit_logs.read_required"}
user: sarah@acme.com

jordan lee: noted. quick checks: is the org_entitlements row populated for acme-42? sometimes SCIM/group sync drops the retention entitlement while leaving audit_read unset. can you run the admin query and paste results? (or i can run if you want me to).

alex kim: pasted output from identity DB (redacted):
```
org_id | entitlement_key            | value
acme-42 | audit_log_read             | false
acme-42 | audit_log_retention       | true
```

alex kim: that looks odd — retention true but read false. they were on a legacy plan until last month and we flipped billing, might be a provisioning mismatch.

maria gomez: if read is false the UI/API will 403. likely SCIM mapping didn't include the admin role after the billing change. jordan, can you flip audit_log_read to true and re-evaluate? will we need cache flush?

ops-esc: taking this. running admin tool now:
```
# grant entitlement via admin tool
./admin-tool grant-entitlement --org acme-42 --entitlement audit_log_read --value true
> OK  (entitlement updated)
# clear internal ent cache for org
./admin-tool clear-cache --org acme-42 --cache entitlements
> OK
```

ops-esc: done. i also double-checked SCIM group sync logs; last sync had 0 errors but the group mapping rule for "infosec" -> audit_admin role was missing after the plan migration. i've re-applied the mapping and triggered a re-sync.

support-bot: Customer notified: request to re-try.

alex kim: customer tried and confirms audit logs load now, API returns 200 and shows events. they also said retention policies are present and older events are visible.

maria gomez: great. can we capture root cause + action items here?

jordan lee: root cause summary: entitlement mismatch after billing migration + SCIM role-mapping omission. action items:
- ensure billing migration job preserves entitlement flags (ENG-789)
- add e2e test for SCIM mapping for audit roles (ENG-790)
- add monitoring alert when org_entitlements.audit_log_read is inconsistent with audit_log_retention (OPS-512)

ops-esc: created ENG-789 for billing migration fix and OPS-512 for the monitor. left notes on ticket #123456 and re-ran entitlement sync.

alex kim: closing on support side, leaving follow-up to eng. customer happy, asked for confirmation email + next steps (sent). :thumbsup:

maria gomez: thanks everyone. i'll add the post-incident blurb to the compliance health doc and link to ENG tickets.

support-bot: Ticket #123456 closed by alex kim. Resolution: entitlement restored; SCIM mapping reapplied; follow-ups created ENG-789, ENG-790, OPS-512.
